items.title: Show HN: I turned my kids' old Yoto Player into an Audiobookshelf player
items.contentSnippet:
My kids love their Yotos and I love Audiobookshelf. I wanted something in between that works as they get older and more control. I had two old Gen 2 players lying around that Yoto no longer supports.
It turns the player into an Audiobookshelf client. You browse your library with the two knobs, the 16x16 screen shows tiny cover art, and favourites and downloads sync back to the server. items.title: Show HN: Sys2txt – transcribe system audio to text in the CLI with a local LLM
items.contentSnippet:
sys2txt is a command line tool that records whatever audio your Linux machine is playing (via PulseAudio/PipeWire's monitor source) and transcribes it live with Whisper, OpenAI's AI-based speech-to-text model.
I use it to caption meetings, videos, and calls playing on my own machine without routing audio through anything else. It supports faster-whisper, openai-whisper, and whisper.cpp (with Vulkan GPU support for AMD), and can either record-then-transcribe once or stream continuously in segment

items.title: Show HN: I got tired of btop not seeing my Mac's chip, so I built siltop
items.contentSnippet:
btop is beautiful. But on my M-series Mac it can't tell me the one thing I actually want to know: what is the chip doing? No watts, no GPU, no per-core clocks.
So I built siltop: btop's calm, with eyes on the silicon. Real power, clocks and temps straight from the SMC and IOReport, no sudo, about 1.3% of one core (btop is ~2.5% on the same machine).
It also tells you what's wrong in plain words ("Busy: rustc using 9.1 cores", "Hot: fans at 80%") before you read a single graph.

items.title: Show HN: I built a free collection of browser-based 3D tools
items.contentSnippet:
I built 3DValley, a collection of free tools for generating and editing 3D models.
You can turn images into 3D models using AI, retexture existing models, remesh geometry, and use other 3D utilities.
Some tools run entirely in your browser, while the more computationally expensive AI models run on shared GPUs with free daily credits.
